nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
ويلا is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «للمطففين» is its khabar (predicate), i.e. a reproach. The accusative is permissible outside the Qur'an, because ويل has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun); the nominative is preferred because no verb from it is uttered, except something irregular (shādhdh) that Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd recited, namely: [al-hazaj] 547-
فما وال ولا واح ... ولا واس أبو هند
(Abū Hind is not one who says "woe", nor "alas", nor "pity".)
If it is derived from a verb, the accusative is preferred according to the grammarians, as in بؤسا له ("misery to him"). If you do not bring the khabar with the first [i.e. with the lām], you use the accusative and say: ويله and ويحه.

nahhas-irab:10-11.t: [الَّذِينَ is] a naʿt (adjective) of المكذبين; the accusative is also permissible, as explained before.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid said: i.e. a transgressor in his speech, a sinner in the sight of his Lord. [Translator's note: the source names him «الحسن بن واقد»; the known transmitter is al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid.]

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: إِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا قالَ أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (13): [أساطير is nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: [بَلْ رانَ] with assimilation (idghām) of the lām into the rāʾ and without inclination (imāla) is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr. Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with assimilation, except that they used imāla. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read بَلْ رانَ without assimilation. Abū Jaʿfar said: Assimilation here is preferable because of the closeness of the lām to the rāʾ, and leaving out imāla is preferable because there is no yāʾ or kasra in it; the imāla is only based on the meaning, since it is from ران يرين, derived from الرّين, as was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿĀrim, who said: I asked al-Aṣmaʿī about the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ «إنه ليغان على قلبي حتى أستغفر الله عزّ وجلّ مائة مرة» ("My heart is clouded over until I ask forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, a hundred times"), and he said: Caution in speaking about the ḥadīth of the Messenger of Allah is like caution about the Qur'an; but the Arabs call a cloud, when it is thin, less than a [full] cloud, الغين and الرّين. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the i'rab and the derivation. As for the meaning, Mujāhid said about it: The heart has fingers; when a servant sins, one finger of it closes, then if he sins another closes, until all of them close and his heart is sealed, so that no admonition benefits it. Abū Jaʿfar said: The best that has been said about this is what is soundly established from the Prophet ﷺ, as was read [in transmission] to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from Qutayba, from al-Layth, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān, from al-Qaʿqāʿ, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, who said: «When the servant commits a sin, a spot is made on his heart — meaning a black one. If he desists, asks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished; and if he goes back, it is increased until it covers his heart. That is the rust (الرين) that Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, mentioned: كَلَّا بَلْ رانَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ (14).»

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: There are two views on its meaning. One of them is that by this He indicated that the believers will not be veiled from looking at Him, Majestic and Mighty is He. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned what Mālik ibn Anas said about that. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about seeing Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, on the Day of Resurrection, and he said: It is indicated by كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ (15). The other view is that the implied form is "from the honour of their Lord", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is wrong according to the school of the grammarians, among them al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; according to them, and according to the other grammarians, it is not permissible to say جاءني زيد ("Zayd came to me") meaning "his servant came to me" or "his honour came to me".

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصالُوا الْجَحِيمِ: [the nūn may be dropped or kept] because it refers to the future. Whoever drops the nūn for lightness says لصالو الجحيمِ in the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); whoever drops it because of the meeting of two vowelless letters puts [الجحيمَ] in the accusative.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: [ثُمَّ يُقالُ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ: the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] of the passive verb, according to Sībawayh, is the clause. He said likewise about ثُمَّ بَدا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما رَأَوُا الْآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ [Yūsuf: 35], [that the clause is] in the position of the fāʿil (agent). This, according to Abū al-ʿAbbās, is a mistake, because a clause does not stand in the place of the agent; rather the verb indicates the maṣdar, and the maṣdar stands in the place of the agent.

nahhas-irab:18-19.t: وَما أَدْراكَ ما عِلِّيُّونَ (19): there are five views about it [i.e. its meaning], and two views about its i'rab. Most of the exegetes, among them Kaʿb, Mujāhid and Zayd ibn Aslam, say: علّيّون is the seventh heaven. Al-Farrāʾ reported that it is the lowest heaven. Qatāda said: [it is] the right leg of the Throne. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: علّيّون is the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary. It was also said: علّيّون are the angels. Abū Jaʿfar said: The majority hold the first view. As for the i'rab, the two views about it are: one of them is that عليين resembles عشرين and the like, because it has no singular; it only means "from height to height", so it was declined like عشرين. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view agrees with the interpretation of those who said علّيّون is the seventh heaven. The other view is that عليين is an adjective of the angels, which is why it was given the sound plural with wāw and nūn.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: الَّذِينَ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المطففين, or in the accusative as censure (ʿalā al-dhamm); the latter is more fitting for the verse. One who is weak in Arabic may imagine that the meaning of اكتلت عليه and اكتلت منه is the same, but their implied senses differ: the meaning of اكتلت عليه is "I took by measure what was due from him", and the meaning of اكتلت منه is "I took my full due from him".

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: That is, that record is a book (كتاب), i.e. something written. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explained that, saying: When the spirit of the believer comes out, the angel takes it and ascends with it to the lowest heaven, and the angels brought near follow it; then likewise from heaven to heaven until he brings it to the seventh heaven, to the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary. There a sealed record from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, reaches them, in which is a security from Allah for so-and-so son of so-and-so from the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and [the tidings] of winning Paradise. Ibn Zayd said: المقربون are the angels.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: It was said: they were called أبرار because of the abundance of truthfulness they practise, because truthfulness is called برّ.

nahhas-irab:23-24.t: عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ (23), i.e. at the palaces, the ḥūr and other things they have. Abū Jaʿfar said: تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ (24): al-Farrāʾ permitted يُعرف, because it [نضرة] is a non-real feminine.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: يُسْقَوْنَ مِنْ رَحِيقٍ مَخْتُومٍ (25): مِنْ رَحِيقٍ is in the position of the accusative as the [second] object of the passive verb, not according to the view of al-Akhfash.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). This is the reading of most people. Al-Kisāʾī read — Abū ʿUbayd related it from him — «خاتمه مسك», and claimed that this reading is the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq mentioned that he found no one who knew this from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. [But] it was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read «خاتمه مسك». Abū Jaʿfar said: ختامه [and خاتمه] have one meaning, except that ختام is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and خاتم is the active participle. Most of the speech of the Arabs regarding people and the like is "he is their خاتم (seal)", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ [al-Aḥzāb: 40], and likewise خاتم; and regarding other than people, ختام, as the poet said: [al-kāmil] 552-
أغلي السّباء بكلّ أدكن عاتق ... أو جونة قدحت وفضّ ختامها
(I pay a high price for wine — every dark, aged [wineskin], or a black jar that is tapped and whose seal is broken.)
وَفِي ذلِكَ فَلْيَتَنافَسِ الْمُتَنافِسُونَ, i.e. let them be eager and seek it. The origin of this is from نفست عليه بالشيء, i.e. I wanted it to be mine rather than his; its derivation is from النّفس, i.e. that in which the soul rejoices and to which it inclines.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t:
عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ (28): there are five views on the accusative of عين. The view of al-Akhfash is that it is accusative by يسقون. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said — ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported it to us — : It is not sound to me that it be accusative except in the sense of أعني ("I mean"). Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "from the تسنيم of a spring", then it was given nunation, so it is put in the accusative, like أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ [al-Balad: 14]. The fourth view: «تسنيم عينا» [i.e. accusative as tamyīz (specification)]. [Translator's note: the source states the fourth view only as «تسنيم عينا»; the bracketed gloss is an interpretation.] The fifth view is that تسنيم is a definite name of the water and عين is indefinite, so it is accusative for that reason. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is the closest to correctness, because it is sound according to the view of the exegetes, as Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar read from Ḥafṣ ibn Yūsuf ibn Mūsā [Translator's note: the isnād appears garbled; elsewhere it runs «Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā».]: Salama narrated to us: Nahshal narrated to us from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said:
«تسنيم» is a spring that flows down (تتسنّم) from the highest part of Paradise; there is no spring in Paradise nobler than it. Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Mujāhid also indicates this; he said: تسنيم is height. Likewise the derivation: one says تسنّمت الماء أتسنّمه تسنيما when I made it flow from a high place, and قبر مسنّم means a raised grave; and from this is the camel's hump (سنام). If someone says: Why is تسنيم declined as a triptote when it is definite, a name of something feminine? It is said: its implied form is that it is a masculine name for the water flowing from that high place; and the meaning of عينا is "flowing", so it has come to be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا, i.e. they earned sin. One says جرم and أجرم when he earned, except that أجرم is more frequent for earning sin, and جرم for other things. الَّذِينَ is the noun (ism) of إنّ; أَجْرَمُوا is its ṣila (relative clause); كانُوا is outside the ṣila because it is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», i.e. they used to be in this world مِنَ الَّذِينَ — those who believed in the oneness of Allah — يَضْحَكُونَ, mocking them. It is related that Abū Jahl and his companions laughed at and mocked ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
The grammarians differed about the position of the hāʾ and mīm [in كالوهم]. Their leading figures — Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and others — said: the position of the hāʾ and mīm is the accusative. This is the school of Sībawayh, by analogy with his saying كلتك ("I measured for you") and صدتك ("I hunted for you"); he does not permit وهبتك, because it is ambiguous, but if you say وهبتك دينارا ("I gave you a dinar") it is permissible. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of the nominative. Abū Ḥātim expressed this by saying that the meaning in his view is: "they, when they measure or weigh, cause loss", because ʿĪsā said: the pause is «وإذا كالوا», then you begin «هم أو وزنوا». Someone else expressed it [by saying] that «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis), as you say قاموا هم. Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct view is that the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of the accusative, because in the written text (السواد) it is without an alif; and the sequence of the speech indicates that, because before it is إِذَا اكْتالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ, so what follows must be "and when they measure for them (كالوا لهم)", the lām being omitted, as [the poet] said — Abū Zayd recited it: [al-kāmil] 548-
ولقد جنيتك أكموءا وعساقلا ... ولقد نهيتك عن بنات الأوبر
(I have gathered for you truffles and ʿasāqil, and I forbade you the [inferior] banāt al-awbar.)
The genitive particle is omitted in what takes two objects, one of them by means of a particle, as the poet said: [al-basīṭ] 549-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I commanded you to do good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
Another said: [al-ṭawīl] 550-
نبّيت عبد الله بالجوّ أصبحت ... كراما مواليها لئيما صميمها
(I was told that ʿAbd Allāh, in al-Jaww, has come to have noble clients but base pure-bred members.)
And another said: [al-basīṭ] 551-
أستغفر الله ذنبا لست محصيه ... ربّ العباد إليه الوجه والعمل ]
(I ask Allah's forgiveness for sins I cannot count — the Lord of the servants, to whom [one turns] one's face and deeds.) [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears at the end of the verse in the source.]

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: ] [Translator's note: the entry begins with a stray bracket in the source.] Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: فاكهين — he is saying: pleased with themselves. Abū Jaʿfar said: That is, pleased with what they were doing and delighted with it. Ibn Zayd said: فاكهين means living in comfort. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that فاكهين [and فكهين] have one meaning. Abū ʿUbayd reported that Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī reported from the Arabs that الفكه is one who laughs much and is good-humoured. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-Aṣmaʿī used to extol Abū Zayd in [matters of] language, mentioning his rank and precedence, and mentioning his truthfulness and trustworthiness. He said: And Khalaf ibn Ḥayyān Abū Muḥriz, despite his eminence, used to attend his circle.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: This is the saying of the disbelievers in this world, i.e. [these] are surely astray from the right path.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: That is, they were not sent to watch over their deeds; they were only commanded to obey Allah the Exalted.

nahhas-irab:34-36.t: فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ (34): that is after they enter Paradise. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Doors to the Fire will be opened for them, and they will look at those who used to mock them in this world and laugh at them; when they see them in the Fire they will rejoice at Allah the Exalted's vengeance on His enemies and laugh at them then, عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ (35) at them. Someone else said: on the couches, looking at their palaces and their spouses, and saying to one another: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ ما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (36). It was also said: هَلْ begins [a new sentence], cut off from what precedes it, i.e. "Have the disbelievers been requited for their deeds?" On this meaning ما is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: أنّ and what it governs are in the position of the two objects.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t:
يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (6): there are several views on its accusative. The implied form may be "will surely be resurrected on the day people stand before the Lord of the worlds". Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: it is like your saying الآن ("now"). Al-Farrāʾ made it indeclinable (mabnī).
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is a mistake, making it indeclinable together with the imperfect verb. In Arabic it is permissible to put it in the genitive as a badal (substitute), and in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). This is what there is of i'rab in it. It was read [in transmission] to Bakr ibn Sahl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf, from ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (6): he said: «They will stand in their sweat up to the middle of their ears.» Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a ḥadīth stated in summary form, with a sound chain of transmission. ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir related it from the Prophet ﷺ in detailed form; he said: «The sun will draw near to the earth on the Day of Resurrection; among people there will be one drowned [in sweat] up to his ankles, one drowned up to the middle of his shins, one drowned up to his shoulders, one drowned up to his neck, one drowned up to the middle of his mouth, bridled by it, and among them one whom the drowning envelops completely.»

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
Whoever says that كَلَّا is a complete stop (tamām) throughout the Qur'an says: the meaning is "the matter is not as the disbelievers suppose, that they will not be resurrected and will not be punished". The scholars spoke about the meaning of سجّين. Abū Hurayra said: سِجِّينٍ is an open pit in Hell. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: «سجين» is beneath the cheek (خدّ) of Iblīs. [Translator's note: the source reads «حد», read here as «خدّ».] It was said: «سجين» is from السجل ("record"), the nūn being a substitute for the lām, i.e. in what has been written against them. Abū ʿUbayda said: في سجين means "in a prison", and it was said that it is from السجن. Some grammarians said: «سجين» is the rock beneath the lowest earth; he claimed that this is related, and that it is an adjective, because if it were a name of the rock it would be a diptote; he said: and you may make it a name of the stone, so you decline it as a triptote. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The best that has been said about سجين is what is soundly established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as was read [in transmission] to Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān, from Ibn Fuḍayl and Abū Muʿāwiya, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl, from Zādhān, from al-Barāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «When the disbelieving — or the wicked — servant dies, his spirit is taken up to the lowest heaven, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, says: Write his record in سِجِّينٍ.» He said:
And it is the lowest earth.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: [وَما أَدْراكَ ما سِجِّينٌ is] for magnification; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: With an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a written record".
